# Daggerheart Coupling Map

**Purpose:** Precise inventory of where Vellum is hardwired to Daggerheart, to target the 0.1.0 composability refactor (`docs/ROADMAP-0.1.0.md`). Generated by a source scan during planning.

## Bottom line

The **plumbing is already generic**: the Context/Provider/hook pattern (`SystemProvider`, `ThemeProvider`), a fully data-driven `StatTrack`, and a `themeToCssVars` reflector all work for any system. Coupling is concentrated in two places:

1. **The type layer** collapses the abstraction to a single concrete system via `SystemConfig = DaggerheartSystemConfig` (and its theme twin). Until that opens up, TypeScript treats every consumer as single-system.
2. **The character model + reducer + parser + the five named stat components** hardcode Daggerheart's specific resource set (hope / fear / hp / stress / armor) as named fields, named actions, and named JSX.

There is **no registry and no system-selection mechanism** anywhere — the active system+theme are chosen once, statically, in `main.tsx`.

---

## 1. System / theme registration seam — LOW–MED effort (blocked by the type layer, not the code)

- `src/systems/SystemContext.ts:4` — `createContext<SystemConfig | null>(null)`. Generic container.
- `src/systems/SystemProvider.tsx:10` — takes a `system` prop; pure pass-through. No registry.
- `src/systems/useSystem.ts:5` — throws if no provider. Fine as-is.
- `src/themes/` mirrors this exactly (`ThemeContext.ts`, `ThemeProvider.tsx:12` applies `themeToCssVars` to `document.documentElement`, `useTheme.ts`).
- Active system+theme chosen **once, statically**, in two places: `src/main.tsx:17-18` and `src/App.test.tsx:14-15` — both hardwire `daggerheartSystem` + `daggerheartTheme`.
- **No registry, no id→config map, no selector.** Provider/context/hook code needs **zero** change to support a 2nd system — the only blocker is the type union in §4.

## 2. Character / state model coupling — HIGH effort (the core of the work)

- `src/character/types.ts:12-18` `CharacterStats` = named DH fields: `hope`, `fear?`, `hp[]`, `stress[]`, `armorSlots[]`. Not generic tracks.
- `:20-24` `CharacterSlotCounts` repeats hp/stress/armorSlots; `:27` `conditions.core` bakes the three DH conditions into the type; `:41` `system: SystemId`.
- `src/character/reducer.ts:4-15` — action set is entirely DH-specific: `HOPE_SET`, `FEAR_SET`, `FEAR_INCREMENT/DECREMENT`, `HP_SET`, `STRESS_SET`, `ARMOR_TOGGLE_SLOT`, `CONDITION_TOGGLE`, `FEATURE_CONDITION_TOGGLE`. Each case reaches into `state.stats.<namedfield>`. → needs generic `TRACK_SET{trackId,…}` actions.
- `src/character/parseCharacter.ts:58-102` — validates each named field literally and loops `CORE_CONDITION_IDS` (`:81`). → must become schema-driven off the SystemConfig.
- `src/character/storage.ts`, `exportCharacter.ts` — **already fully generic** (opaque JSON round-trip; export only reads `identity.name`). No change.
- `src/character/fixtures.ts:6` + `CharacterProvider.tsx` — provider generic; fixture hardcodes `system:'daggerheart'` + DH identity.

## 3. Component coupling — MED effort

- **Fully generic (the reuse primitive):** `src/components/StatTrack/StatTrack.tsx` — props-driven: `label`, `trackLength`, `currentValue`, `shape` (pip/box/heart), `interaction` (level/toggle), `tone`, `thresholds`, callbacks. Renders any track.
- **DH-named wrappers, each hardwired** (label + tone + shape + which field/action): `PlayerHud/Hope.tsx`, `HP.tsx`, `Stress.tsx`, `Armor.tsx`, `GmHud/Fear.tsx`. E.g. `Hope.tsx:11-18` hardcodes `label="Hope"`, `tone="var(--color-gold)"`, `system.hope.max`, `HOPE_SET`.
- **`src/components/PlayerHud/PlayerHud.tsx:13-16` hardcodes the roster** `<HP/><Hope/><Stress/><Armor/>` — no data-driven "render the system's tracks" loop. **Key generalization point:** a system-declared track list + one generic `<Track>` replaces all five wrappers + this roster.
- `ConditionsPanel.tsx:29` — **already generic** (maps `system.coreConditions` + `character.featureConditions`). The template to copy.
- `HpThresholds.tsx:17-56` — DH damage tiers (Minor/Major/Severe = 1/2/3 HP) hardcoded in JSX; DH-specific mechanic → system-optional widget.
- `IdentityLabel.tsx` — class/ancestry/subclass/community/level; DH-flavored but soft (generic strings).
- `CharacterSetup.tsx:36-38,79` — form hardcodes DH fields + defaults (`hp:6, stress:6, armorSlots:3, hope:2`) and `system:'daggerheart'` (the runtime write path — new characters are always DH).

## 4. Every hardcoded `'daggerheart'` / SYSTEM_IDS / DH constant (runtime, non-test)

- `src/systems/types.ts:4` `SYSTEM_IDS = ['daggerheart'] as const`
- **`src/systems/types.ts:22` `export type SystemConfig = DaggerheartSystemConfig`** ← the single most load-bearing line; collapses the union to one system.
- `src/systems/types.ts:11-12` `interface DaggerheartSystemConfig { readonly id: 'daggerheart'; … }`
- `src/systems/types.ts:1` `CORE_CONDITION_IDS = ['hidden','restrained','vulnerable']`
- `src/themes/types.ts:47,54` `id: 'daggerheart'` + `type ThemeConfig = DaggerheartThemeConfig` (same collapse, theme side)
- `src/systems/daggerheart.system.ts:3-4` / `src/themes/daggerheart.theme.ts:3-4` — the config objects
- `src/main.tsx:7,9,17,18` — imports + provider props
- `src/character/fixtures.ts:6` `system:'daggerheart'`
- `src/components/CharacterSetup/CharacterSetup.tsx:79` `system:'daggerheart'`
- `src/dice/rollDuality.ts:1` `import { roll } from '@randsum/daggerheart'`; `package.json` dep `@randsum/daggerheart@1.1.1`
- **Dead weight:** `SystemConfig.hpClassTable` + `armorTable` (`daggerheart.system.ts:9-26`) are defined + unit-tested but **consumed by no runtime component** (only `coreConditions` is used). CharacterSetup takes raw slot counts instead.

## 5. Dice roller — MED effort, cleanly isolated

- `src/dice/rollDuality.ts` is entirely DH (Duality Hope/Fear d12s, advantage d6, outcomes hope/fear/critical-hope), a thin typed seam over `@randsum/daggerheart`.
- Wired: `dice/index.ts` → `DiceRoller.tsx:3` → `GmHud.tsx:3` (GM HUD always renders it). `DiceRoller.tsx` UI hardcodes duality concepts (`OUTCOME_LABEL:11`, Hope/Fear dice `:56-58`, advantage modes `:5`).
- To generalize: SystemConfig owns an optional dice/roller descriptor; DiceRoller renders from it. Systems without dice omit it.

## 6. Tests that must change for a 2nd system

- `daggerheart.system.test.ts` — stays as the DH suite (add a parallel per system).
- `character/template.test.ts` — asserts `system==='daggerheart'`.
- `dice/rollDuality.test.ts:5` — `vi.mock('@randsum/daggerheart')`.
- **Every component test** wraps in `<SystemProvider system={daggerheartSystem}>` — needs a shared test helper taking an arbitrary system, but does **not block** a 2nd system.
- `themes/no-hardcoded-values.test.ts` — **not system-coupled** (scans CSS for hardcoded colors). No change.

---

## Ranked blockers to adding a 2nd system (do top-first)

1. **`src/systems/types.ts:22` `SystemConfig = DaggerheartSystemConfig`** (+ theme twin `themes/types.ts:54`). Open to a discriminated union / interface keyed by `id`. Everything else depends on this.
2. **`src/character/types.ts` `CharacterStats` / `conditions.core`** — named DH fields → generic keyed track/resource maps. Ripples into reducer, parser, fixtures, every stat component.
3. **`src/character/reducer.ts` action set** — DH-named actions → generic `TRACK_SET{trackId}` / `CONDITION_TOGGLE{id}`.
4. **`PlayerHud.tsx:13-16` roster + the 5 named wrappers** — replace with a system-declared track list rendered through the already-generic `StatTrack`. `ConditionsPanel` is the model.
5. **`parseCharacter.ts` field-by-field validation** — derive from the SystemConfig track schema.
6. **No registry / selection layer** — `SYSTEM_IDS`, static `main.tsx` wiring, `CharacterSetup.tsx:79`. Add an id→config registry + active-system persistence.
7. **Dice** — isolate `rollDuality` + DiceRoller + the `@randsum/daggerheart` dep behind a system-owned roller descriptor.
8. **`HpThresholds`** — system-optional widget or generalized.

**Cheapest early win:** the plumbing already proves the pattern (`StatTrack` + `ConditionsPanel` are data-driven), and `hpClassTable`/`armorTable` are declared-but-unread — so the generalization has a real foothold. The heavy lift is the character model (#2/#3), not the provider seam.
